notes.title: Planetbase 2 Evolution
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

As you might know, we are now working on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3509420/Planetbase_2/]Planetbase 2[/url]. We've just posted [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3509420/view/516337874624316081]Dev Update 01[/url] if you want to check the progress so far.

Much like [b]Dawn of Man[/b] was a spiritual successor to [b]Planetbase[/b], [b]Planetbase 2[/b] now continues adding on top of the feature set available in [b]Dawn of Man[/b].

A lot of the best features in DoM will be making a comeback, we want players to feel at home right away when playing the game.


[h2]Direct controls and multi-select[/h2]

Much like in Dawn of Man, in Planetbase 2 you will be able to select a bunch of people and tell them to [i]go someplace[/i], go [i]work in a particular structure[/i] or go [i]perform a particular task[/i].

The game will try very hard to make micromanagement tasks as few and far between as possible, but sometimes you just need to tell colonists exactly what to do.


[h2]Work areas and complex resource limits[/h2]

You will be able to place [i]Work Areas[/i], each associated with a [i]number of workers[/i] and a [i]resource limit[/i].
Resource limits can be [i]absolute[/i], or expressed as a [i]percentage [/i]of the total population.
The difference is that instead of [i]Sticks[/i], [i]Fish [/i]or [i]Crops[/i], you will be mining [i]Ice[/i], [i]Regolith[/i], [i]Iron Ore[/i] or [i]Silica[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/7ace49ab36e12660bb8b17227a6972ef2497cb27.png[/img]


[h2]Realistic character proportions[/h2]

In Planetbase 2, we are are moving away from the more cartoony character style we used for Planetbase 1 and we are using using Dawn of Man's character proportions, to achieve a more realistic look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/63b926ec474fe09fe294f6eca4ae638b0be44188.png[/img]


[h2]Transports and Machinery[/h2]

In Dawn of man you have [i]Sledges[/i], [i]Carts[/i], and [i]Plows[/i], in Planetbase 2 we will have [i]Rovers[/i], [i]Trucks[/i], [i]Mining Vehicles[/i] and [i]Tankers[/i].
There is obviously not a 1 to 1 match here, but vehicle management and construction will be a big part of the gameplay in Planetbase 2, like it is in Dawn of Man.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/ae82d175a5c544ecaa90c88807ea9302725c017b.png[/img]

We will post updates every 2-3 months on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3509420/Planetbase_2/]Steam[/url], but if you want to stay more up to date with the development you can follow us on [url=https://x.com/madrugaworks]X[/url] or [url=https://madrugaworks.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url], we post several times a week there.

Thank you everyone for your support!

Martiño.

notes.title: Planetbase 2 Announcement
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

We can now announce that we've started work on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3509420/Planetbase_2/]Planetbase 2[/url]. As much that this is a sequel to the original [b]Planetbase[/b], this is also [b]Dawn of Man[/b]'s spiritual successor, the theme changes, but the city-builder/RTS/survival concept remains.

A ton of features from [b]Dawn of Man[/b] like [i]work areas[/i], [i]relative resource limits[/i], [i]direct RTS style commands[/i] or [i]storage filters[/i] will be making a comeback in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3509420/Planetbase_2/]Planetbase 2[/url],

After [b]10 years[/b], now the time has come to go back to our origins and [b]revisit the Planetbase idea[/b]. We now have the time and resources to expand a concept that we always thought had a [b]lot more potential[/b].

[previewyoutube=eL_VGHLvpzg;full][/previewyoutube]
We've started work on this about 6 months ago, and we are still very much working out the exact design for the game, but these are the core ideas are focusing on:

[h3]Real worlds[/h3]
In Planetbase, the planets were inspired by real worlds of the solar system, but we stopped short of calling them by their names.
Now we want to add a more [i]realistic[/i] twist (if you can call the colonization of the Solar System realistic) and allow the player to colonize real worlds. 
We are initially working on [b]Mars[/b], but other worlds worlds we have in mind are [i]The Moon[/i], [i]Europa [/i]or [i]Titan[/i].

[h3]Tech Tree[/h3]
In Planetbase you could acquire some techs, but now we are adding a proper tech tree like in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/858810/Dawn_of_Man/]Dawn of Man[/url]. Where it makes sense you will be able to research new technologies, and if we are talking about things that couldn't be researched in an off planet-colony you will be able to buy the right patents to use them.

[h3]Vehicles[/h3]
Off world colonization won't be possible without using vehicles. We are working on adding [b]rovers[/b], [b]mining vehicles[/b] or [b]propellant tankers[/b]. These will be instrumental to increase the [b]efficiency [/b]of your base.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/10221286/bc6a805511fe98a0a946acc3b0de0c43f91dfe40.png[/img]

[h3]Complex production chains[/h3]
We want to expand on the simple ideas we had in Planetbase for resource gathering and manufacturing, allowing the player to mine in-situ resources and go in more detail about what would be required to create a self sustaining off-world manufacturing industry.

[h3]New power and water sources[/h3]
The power/water mechanics in PB1 were pretty simple, we now want to add more complex power and water mechanics. Things like actively mining and [b]melting ice[/b] to produce water, building an maintain [b]nuclear reactors[/b], survey the planet surface searching for the right area to place a [b]geothermal[/b] plant and more....

[h3]Separate bases[/h3]
This is an idea we always had in mind, we really need to think through how the player will be able to control this from the gameplay point of view, but we want to enable construction of separate bases and power grids.

[h3]RTS features[/h3]
All the RTS style features like multi-selection and direct commands from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/858810/Dawn_of_Man/]Dawn of Man[/url] will be making a comeback.

[h3]Devlog[/h3]
This time around we've decided to announce the game much earlier, instead of working in the dark for years in order to gather feedback and engage with the community. We will be publishing a devlog with regular updates on [url=x.com/madrugaworks]X[/url] and [url=madrugaworks.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url].

Thank you everyone for joining us in this amazing journey!
Martiño.

notes.title: Version 1.8.0 released
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

We've finally managed to spare some time from the development of our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2281940/The_Mobius_Machine/]new project[/url] to release [b]version 1.8.0[/b].

The game now runs on the latest Unity stable version (2022.3 ATM). 
We've been wanting to upgrade for a while, but unfortunately this wasn't a trivial task, as there were some changes in the [i]random[/i] and [i]math[/i] libraries, that were breaking our procedural map generation.
It took us a while, but we got everything sorted out and managed to upgrade.
This should provide better compatibility across the board for newer systems.

[h3]New Grass/Reed rendering[/h3]
Grass and reed details, are now rendered as geometry instead of billboards, and they are also using different shaders to the rest of the terrain details.
They now look nicer, provide more coverage, and blend better with the terrain.

[h3]Terrain Shadows[/h3]
In High and Ultra quality modes, terrain now casts shadows, see the difference in this screenshots:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/c51516583d27222824aa95d67323eaec4980b667.png[/img]

[h3]New Fullscreen Modes[/h3]
You can now select [i]Exclusive[/i] fullscreen mode in settings screen, this provides an alternative to anyone that might be experiencing issues with the current [i]Borderless [/i] mode.
On Mac we are also now supporting [i]Maximized [/i]mode. 

[h3]Other changes[/h3]
- Disabling IMGUI layouts, which saves random memory allocations.
- Removed duplicate string warnings for workshop scenarios.
- Updated Madruga Works logo.
- Better handling of some OneDrive errors.

We want to take this chance to thank everyone in the community that supported us and allows us to keep on making games!

Martiño.

notes.title: Version 1.7 released | Cheese Update
notes.content:
In this update we are adding Cheesemaking, some improvements to animal trading and a bunch of other fixes.

[h1]Cheese[/h1]
[b]Cheese[/b] can now be made in the new [b]Cheesemaker[/b] structure, from the Neolithic onward. 
Cheese lasts for longer than Milk, and can be traded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/39fa371bf62783012d7c4ceeaf839da102a01117.jpg[/img]

[h1]Trading[/h1]
- You can now sell animals to trader.
- Trader can now bring male and female animals at the same time, and you can choose which ones to purchase.
- Trader animals are now visible and stay in village when purchased, or leave when sold.
- Main trader that comes to village can now sometimes be an old person and companion trader can be of any age.
- Male animals are now cheaper.

[h1]Misc[/h1]
- When double clicking on animals, only animals from the same team are selected (Trader or Player).
- Default resource limit for sickles is now 75% of adults.

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
- Edit work area option doesn't appear when several Work Areas are selected.
- When editing a work area, canceling caused the work area to be destroyed. Now, the work area will be restored to its original location.
- Fix for issue that could potentially result in people being stuck after coming down from platforms.

notes.title: Version 1.6 released | Armor Update
notes.content:
This update focuses on some of the main feature requests from the community, which were Armor and combat improvements.

[h1]Highlights[/h1]

[b]ARMOR[/b]

Your people can now make armor, they will automatically equip it when you sound the alarm. Note that raiders will also wear armor, from the Bronze Age onward.

Armor is made in the new [b]Armorer[/b] structure, we've also moved shield production there (which was previously in the Workshop).

It comes in two variants, Leather Armor, available from the Bronze Age, and Mail Armor, available from the Iron Age.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/d8b22731b654315cbb8fd263061f6a5c0c1c6f12.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/f3fdb481c55af955ca641f64996d2fb28922b208.png[/img]


[b]GATE RALLY POINTS[/b]

You can now choose the position where your people gather when you trigger the alert.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/1019c45b50a97ca40994ec3604b5a1d46eee5333.png[/img]


[b]GATES IN 8 DIRECTIONS[/b]

You can now place gates in 8 directions, allowing for much more organic looking towns.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/5acfd64edd480717f6afff37b8df23354b083605.png[/img]


[b]WALLS IN SHALLOW WATER[/b]

Walls can now be built in shallow water (and steeper slopes), this makes it possible to use lakes and rivers as defensive barriers. Raiders might end up swimming through them to attack you, but this would still allow you to shoot at them from a distance for a long time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/c3c44dbeab9aab9350878ebdd4e33ea91b1077cc.png[/img]


[h1]Full Changelog[/h1]

[b]NEW RESOURCE: LEATHER ARMOR[/b]
Made from leather, offers reasonable protection, available from the Bronze Age.

[b]NEW RESOURCE: MAIL ARMOR[/b]
Made from iron rings, offers very good protection, available in the Iron Age.

[b]NEW STRUCTURE: ARMORER[/b]
Structure that produces Leather and Mail Armor, we've also moved the shield manufacturing here, which was in the Workshop previously.

[b]NEW TECHS[/b]
New techs [b]Armor[/b], [b]Mail[/b] and [b]Reinforced Shields[/b], required for Leather Armor, Mail Armor and Oval Shields.

[b]COMBAT IMPROVEMENTS[/b]
- It is now possible to edit the position at which people gather behind the gates when the alert is on.
- Gates can now be build in 8 directions allowing for more organic wall designs.
- You can now build walls, watchtowers and platforms in shallow water, and in steeper slopes.
- In the Bronze and Iron Ages, raiders don't immediately acquire all techs in the era, but they do it progressively with each attack wave.
- There is now an option in the defense panel to customize the amount of men and women that will use melee weapons in combat.
- People will now upgrade their weapons from slings to bows if available.
- Weapons that raiders drop when dead now have random condition instead of 100%
- Added some old raiders, and slightly increased the proportion of males that come to attack.
- Clothing now decays when absorbing combat damage, the damage that is saved is instead taken by the clothing.
- Stamina decay rate is now cut in half when the alert is on. This affects all humans, including raiders.
- Slings can now be sold for their full value up to the Neolithic only (down from the Copper Age).
- Making sure that people don't run to another gate after all raiders are dead.
- Animals that have been butchered, even only partially, now decay a lot faster.
- Most defensive structures, like walls, gates and towers are now a bit more resistant.

[b]NEW ADULT PERCENTAGE RESOURCE LIMITS[/b]
- It is now possible to set a resource limit to a percentage of the adults in the settlement.
- This is now the default for tools, shields and armor, as children can not use them.
- Improved tooltips for all resource limits, to make everything more clear.
- Added 20% and 33% resource limits

[b]IMPROVED HUNTING RESOURCE LIMITS[/b]
- Butchering tasks for hunted or slaughtered animals will now only get auto-generated if any of Meat, Bone or Raw Skins are under the limits.
- In auto generated butchering tasks (after hunting or slaughtering), people will not extract resources that are over the limits.
- Meat limit is now set to 100 by default (it was 30 before).
- Raw Skins limit is now set to 40 by default (it was 10 before).
- Bones limit is now set to 20 by default (it was 10 before).
- These changes do not affect manual butcher tasks (created by right clicking or using the context actions), these always extract all resources from the animal.

[b]IMPROVED COMBAT BEHAVIOUR[/b]
When a person is given a direct command to move somewhere (by right clicking on the ground), they will stay there and:
- They won't go to their usual combat positions. This is useful when the enemies are attacking if you want to station a bunch of people somewhere instead of in the default positions.
- They won't wander around town.
- For a while, they won't go and get any weapons or armor.
- For a while, they won't go to rest.
- For a while, they won't get assigned any tasks.
- For a while, they won't go store any resources.
The idea behind these changes is that you get more control over what people do, but eventually they will do what they need to do to survive.

[b]IMPROVED PATHFINDING[/b]
- Humans will retry with higher accuracy if they can't find a suitable path to the destination.
- Beings prefer to walk on even terrain.
- Beings try harder to cross by a nearby ford instead of swimming.

[b]MISC[/b]
- New loading screen for the Ancient Warriors scenario.
- Ancient Warriors tech cost has now been slightly reduced.
- Slightly increased population limit.
- Domestic Animals will now prefer to wander around stables.
- People now prefer to wear outfits that are in better condition.
- Workload calculations now count kids as half an adult.
- You can now select a loaded person and right click on a storage structure to tell them to unload there.
- Added Elasmotherium, Hyena, long haired woman and old man to intro screen.
- Carts, Sledges and Plows can now be built by two people simultaneously.

Meat limit is now set to 100 by default (it was 30 before).
Raw Skins limit is now set to 40 by default (it was 10 before).
Bones limit is now set to 20 by default (it was 10 before).
These changes do not affect manual butcher tasks (created by right clicking or using the context actions), these always extract all resources from the animal.

When a person is given a direct command to move somewhere (by right clicking on the ground), they will stay there and:
- They won't go to their usual combat positions. This is useful when the enemies are attacking if you want to station a bunch of people somewhere instead of in the default positions.
- They won't wander around town.
- For a while, they won't go and get any weapons or armor.
- For a while, they won't go to rest.
- For a while, they won't get assigned any tasks.
- For a while, they won't go store any resources.
The idea behind these changes is that you get more control over what people do, but eventually they will do what they need to do to survive.
Humans will retry with higher accuracy if they can't find a suitable path to the destination.
Beings prefer to walk on even terrain.
Beings try harder to cross by a nearby ford instead of swimming.
New loading screen for the Ancient Warriors scenario.
Ancient Warriors tech cost has now been slightly reduced.
Slightly increased population limit.
Domestic Animals will now prefer to wander around stables.
People now prefer to wear outfits that are in better condition.
Workload calculations now count kids as half an adult.
You can now select a loaded person and right click on a storage structure to tell them to unload there.
Added Elasmotherium, Hyena, long haired woman and old man to intro screen.
Carts, Sledges and Plows can now be built by two people simultaneously.

notes.title: Console version and future updates
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

Now that 2019 is coming to an end, we want to take a moment to thank the [b]Dawn of Man community[/b]. The game wouldn't be the same without your continued feedback, bug reports, workshop content, and overall support! Thanks!

Dawn of Man has been a success beyond our expectations. We are very glad people are enjoying the game, and for a moment, they can feel like they are transported thousands of years to the amazing time that was the beginning of humanity.

[h1]Console version[/h1]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/df84883434d8a92f08c0a602ddc269134c8b5ef5.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/626c050895267daaa829c960e060dc8fccd9240c.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Future Updates[/h1]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/c7b2218ad0e96f11ae82f1bce30d16ef28c6f43c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/316d4e94dfc208b2816761d0c0d9769cd6328e5e.png[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/0a19a2bc43dac6cf17065c915a060046c5efedfc.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/ddf37b18977e29663249df641e5ada1598a53d14.png[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/e39424a7b149bb3d1cd8abb508c6e5e05f46650b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/409b63fd8e27d4774e2ec0dfb2de1244585c7c91.png[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/93f96fe19a1784e81f2204b67321fbd32dd07f77.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/df9e089aad22d2400232545f8b956aaef2f0b8a7.png[/img][/url]

notes.content:
This is a new major update that adds [i]burial[/i] mechanics to the game.

[h1]Burials[/h1]
When people die, they will get taken to a burial structure and mourned. 
This process allows people to recover the morale they lost when that person died.
There is a new [b]Burial Mound[/b] structure, and the existing [b]Dolmen[/b] and [b]Cairn[/b] buildings have been repurposed as funerary structures as well.

A small tomb where to bury your dead.

Rebalanced danger levels and the amount of hunters that go to attack each type of animal.
Fixed issue with hunt work area tasks always sending 1-3 hunters.

notes.title: Version 1.3.2 released
notes.content:
In this update we've made some changes to the AI, in order to make it cope better with high workload situations. 

Managing the workload of your settlement is still important in order for people to prioritize tasks correctly, but now this should never result in people dying of starvation or dehydration.

- For any task to be assigned to a human, they have to have at least 50% hydration (this could be 25% before in some cases).

- If someone is crafting a non-food item, and their nutrition or hydration go too low, they will abort.
- There are a few more situations where people will abort what they are doing if they are low on hydration or nutrition.
- When cutting down trees using a Sledge/Cart the resulting logs will always be placed in the transport and not the person's inventory.
- Collect tannin and flax tasks now have the same priority as all other non-food related collection tasks (before their priority was the same as of food tasks, which was higher).

[h1]Misc[/h1]
- Fixed typo in the "Resource has decayed" French text
- Fixed a couple of rare crashes
- Fixed bug which would allow the player to place the second variant of the tent in an isolated location, causing different issues
- When the game fails to open the profile or settings files, it now gives a more helpful error

notes.title: Version 1.3 released | Fauna content update
notes.content:
This is a large content update focusing on the new [i]Nomad Mode[/i], more animals and overhauling the fauna and hunting mechanics overall.
More frequent updates in our [url=twitter.com/madrugaworks]devlog[/url].

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jhs1C-tVFH0

[h1]Nomad mode[/h1]
In nomad mode you get [b]no initial structures[/b], but you get [b]extra building materials and food[/b].
All resources are located in your people's inventory for ease of transport.
This way you can move your people around the map before settling and choose a different location for your village.
[b]All Freeplay[/b] scenarios are playable in nomad mode.


[h1]New animals[/h1]
[b]Cave Hyena[/b]
A medium sized predator, available in all freeplay scenarios.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32831408/9b52597251afadaa3f89631004b411f6e5fd06ad.jpg[/img]

[b]Elasmotherium[/b]
An extinct genus of large rhinoceros, available in [i]The Northlands[/i] scenario.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32831408/e1e8dfebd3eb94bbec5d42a5cd3ffe5e62c61bfa.png[/img]

[b]Muskox[/b] 
A large herbivore, available in [i]The Northlands[/i] scenario.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32831408/9ff19d41c80a5d6411c8d0a34d5814b51f993523.jpg[/img]

[b]Feral Horse[/b] 
In the Iron Age, all wild horses went extinct, and horses roaming the wild were feral instead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/c92ff95d5a80d651c6faa83a3cb730944aae0b64.png[/img]

[h1]New techs[/h1]
[b]Dog Training[/b] - Allows dogs to help with hunting.
[b]Bone Polishing[/b] - Unlocks Bone Knife and Bone Sickle.

[h1]New bone tools[/h1]
New bone tools make [i]bone[/i] more useful early game, as it typically was too abundant, these include the [i]Bone Knife[/i] and [i]Bone Sickle[/i]

[h1]Fauna behavior overhaul[/h1]
The behaviour of wild animals is now more realistic making gameplay more challenging and interesting.

- Animals defend all young around the area, not just their own offspring (this makes Wolves and Cave Lions quite a bit more aggressive).
- Animals sometimes disengage from the attacker if it runs away (unless hungry). Humans will now run away when confronted with overwhelming odds.
- Animals will now try really hard not to drink near the player's settlement.
- Animals will now react properly while drinking when attacked by other animals.
- Animals won't eat dead animals that have butcher tasks associated with them.
- Several herbivores might retaliate when attacking their herd, even in normal mode.
- Animals now target humans more often when hungry (but still prefer other animals).
- Dogs can be knocked back by large animals.

[h1]Balance changes[/h1]
- All outfits now take 90s to make (up from 50 or 60).
- All flint tools now take 60s to make (up from 50).
- All bone tools last for less time and uses when compared with the equivalent flint tools.
- All animals have had their speeds, produced resources and hit points reviewed and iterated.
- Downgrading [i]Food Dryer[/i] to 6 slots, this will force the player to build more of these, as they were too efficient before.
- Doubled the amount of time animal carcasses remain in the game.
- Cave Lions now do 35 damage (from 30).

[h1]Work Area management improvements[/h1]
- Added work areas panel.
- Replaced Next/Previous work area buttons in work area options by a button to access the panel (Next/Previous work area shortcuts still work).

notes.content:
This version adds quite a few improvements based on community feedback: More population in late game, AI, QoL and transport management improvements.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

[b]AI Improvements.[/b]
- Children can now milk goats and cows.
- Stricter enforcement of animals limits: more slaughter tasks get generated if required.
- When people go back to town to rest, change outfit, or get better tools, they won't drop their current sledge if carrying one.
- People now prefer to use carts over sledges if available.
- Preventing people from wandering around town immediately after delivering a resource to storage, so they can store more resources faster.
- Fixed issue where AI would not use transports if going to grab one more resource than they can carry.

[b]Balance changes.[/b]
- Relaxing population limits, you can now get more people in your settlement.
- Structures now have custom amounts at which they give knowledge points, in order to promote reasonable settlement construction. Residence structures give more points, crafting and mining structures give less.
- Added move speed modifiers for transports, depending on how full they are: 90% - 70% for sledges, 95% - 75% for donkey carts, 100% - 80% for horse carts.
- Increased the amount of wolves in paleolithic and mesolithic

[b]Notification changes.[/b]
- When continuous production of Carts or Sledges is active, you don't get notifications about them decaying anymore.
- Once you build 3 stables, you stop getting notifications of animal births or deaths by slaughtering.

notes.title: Announcing Dawn of Man
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32831408/9a5d67a10e891e8906882bebe27b57513efcdfe0.png[/img][/img]

We are announcing our new title, [b]Dawn of Man[/b]!

The game is a spiritual successor to our previous title [b]Planetbase[/b], but set in a period of time starting about [b]12,000 years ago[/b], when the last glacial period ended and human populations started to grow.

You will begin controlling a small hunter-gatherer camp, then expand and evolve until the dawn of history. You will have to face the same challenges our ancestors did, thousands of years ago.

[h1]Features[/h1]

Dawn of Man features mechanics that are somewhat inspired by Planetbase but with quite a few differences (we are coding the game from scratch).
[list]
	[*] You will be able to research [b]new techs[/b], to take your people from the Paleolithic up to the Iron Age.
	[*] You will be able to [b]micromanage[/b] them in detail (this is optional, you will still be able to do overall planning of the settlement).
	[*] The game will be quite a bit longer, about twice the size of Planetbase.
	[*] The environment plays a big role, you will have to learn how to deal with the different animals in order to [b]hunt[/b], [b]domesticate[/b], or [b]defend[/b] against them.
	[*] [b]Combat[/b] is still not the main focus in the game, but plays an increased role, you will have to fortify your village and defend it against attacks.
[/list]
